summary: You have produced a well-structured, clearly written report that establishes a strong Australian context and rationale for monitoring the Great Barrier Reef. Your Gantt chart provides a solid foundation for your schedule. To progress to the higher rubric levels, you need to develop concrete functional and mission requirements, incorporate risk and contingency planning, resolve a fundamental orbital mechanics error regarding geostationary altitudes, and produce actual technical modeling or calculation outputs.
next_steps: Correct your orbital design: replace the 'geostationary orbit at 600 km' concept with an astrodynamically viable orbit (e.g., GEO at ~35,786 km, or a Low Earth Orbit suited for Earth observation).
Generate initial technical modeling outputs in STK or mathematical calculations (such as coverage, revisit time, or link budgets) to provide tangible preliminary progress.
Expand the project plan to incorporate contingency strategies, risk management, and formal references to technical textbooks, standards, or databases.

criteria.C1: You clearly articulated the user needs and context for reef monitoring in 'Mission Concept & Rationale'. To reach Accomplished, define detailed, measurable functional and technical requirements rather than broad concepts, ensuring complete mission requirements link directly to specific operational parameters.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart (Image 1) effectively maps out key tasks to demonstrate basic feasibility. For Accomplished, integrate explicit risk analysis and contingency plans for project variations, and link your schedule steps directly to technical information sources and literature.
criteria.C3: Completing tutorials and background reading shows initiative, but no technical results were submitted. To achieve Adequate or Accomplished, include initial preliminary calculations, orbital simulations, or sensor feasibility estimates along with brief interpretation and discussion of your findings.
criteria.C4: Your presentation was clear, well-structured, and easy to read, with neat figures. Maintain this high standard while replacing bare URL footnotes with formal, complete bibliographic citations throughout your future submissions.
